decision: Preserve live durable worker leases when a new qrexec service process restores MissionQueue state.
problem: The qrexec service is process-per-call. Restoring a running mission with preserveRunningLeasesOnRestore=false requeues it before a later heartbeat/complete/fail request can prove the same fenced authority, even when the lease is still live and the leaseToken is correct.

independentReviews.preferredApproach: set preserveRunningLeasesOnRestore=true at the qrexec service boundary
independentReviews.reason: Process-per-call transport must preserve the durable workerId, leaseToken, and live leaseUntil across service invocations or fenced follow-up mutations are impossible. Expired leases still requeue through existing restore/requeue logic.

independentReviews.preferredApproach: preserve only live durable leases and continue requiring exact leaseToken fencing
independentReviews.reason: This does not weaken stale-worker rejection. It keeps authority only when durable ownership metadata exists and leaseUntil remains in the future; stale or expired leases still fail/requeue.

independentReviews.preferredApproach: reuse MissionQueue restore semantics instead of a long-lived qrexec daemon
independentReviews.reason: Adds no extra round trip, daemon, database, IPC channel, or persistent process state. It changes only restore policy for the qrexec adapter and preserves the existing file format.

alternativesRejected.approach: leave restore recovery at the default and reclaim on every qrexec call
alternativesRejected.reason: Breaks heartbeat/complete/fail across process-per-call boundaries and invalidates lease-token authority.

alternativesRejected.approach: run a long-lived qrexec coordinator daemon
alternativesRejected.reason: Avoids restore but adds lifecycle, memory, IPC, crash-state, and attack surface that is unnecessary when live leases can be restored safely.

alternativesRejected.approach: disable lease-token fencing for qrexec follow-up calls
alternativesRejected.reason: Would weaken security and allow stale workers to mutate missions.

qaRequirements: claim in one qrexec process, heartbeat in a second, and complete in a third using the same live leaseToken
verify every response with request-bound Ed25519 attestation
verify durable final mission state is completed after reopen
retain existing expired-lease and stale-token rejection tests
keep requireLeaseToken=true at the service boundary
failuresLessons: Process-per-call transport changes restore semantics into part of the protocol contract; a restart policy suitable for crash recovery is not automatically suitable for every normal qrexec invocation.
Lease preservation is safe only together with expiry checks and exact fencing-token verification.
